$comment: Licence facts that vcpkg cannot supply, plus the decisions that are ours rather than
observations: which licence we ELECT for a dual-licensed component, and where the
Entries with origin != 'vcpkg' are components that never appear in vcpkg.json because
they do not come from vcpkg. They are still SHIPPED, so they are still audited -- the
GCC runtime above all, since it is the one GPL-family licence present in every binary
we produce, and it is allowed only by its Runtime Library Exception.
Tech-Stack-Plan.md 6.2 and 8.1 own these facts. This file is their machine-readable form.

qt.sourceOffer: TODO-BEFORE-RELEASE: host the exact Qt 6.11.1 source tarball and any patch series at a stable URL, and link it from About -> Third-Party Notices (Tech-Stack-Plan.md 8.1).
qt.election: Qt is taken under LGPL-3.0, linked dynamically and shipped as replaceable DLLs. Never -static; never signature-locked or anti-tampered.

gcc-runtime.election: libstdc++-6.dll, libgcc_s_seh-1.dll and libwinpthread-1.dll are shipped beside the executable, never statically linked. The Runtime Library Exception permits distributing a program under any licence, INCLUDING PROPRIETARY, provided it was produced by an Eligible Compilation Process -- i.e. stock GCC with no non-free plugin. TA-9 and license-audit both check that condition.

mingw-w64-runtime.election: The mingw-w64 runtime is a permissive mix (public domain / ZPL-2.1 / MIT / BSD-2) recorded per component. Zlib is used here as the representative expression; the per-component breakdown is owed before release.

pdfium.election: Consumed as a DLL through its FPDF_ C API (verified T12, 2026-08-18), so the compiler that built it does not matter. Read and raster only -- every write goes through our own COS layer. NOTE: the prebuilt archive ships only the packager MIT licence; PDFium own BSD-3-Clause text and its third-party notices must be fetched into res/licenses/ before release.

freetype.election: FreeType is dual-licensed FTL / GPL-2.0. We ELECT FTL. FTL requires a credit in the documentation, which the Third-Party Notices dialog provides.

hunspell.sourceOffer: TODO-BEFORE-RELEASE: host the exact Hunspell source and any patch we apply, alongside the Qt source offer, and link both from About -> Third-Party Notices.
hunspell.election: Hunspell is tri-licensed 'MPL-1.1 OR LGPL-2.1-or-later OR GPL-2.0-or-later' (verified against upstream license.hunspell and vcpkg's port manifest, 2026-08-18). We ELECT the LGPL branch, and because that grant is '2.1 OR LATER' we take it specifically as LGPL-3.0 -- the same licence as Qt. That means one obligation model covers both libraries: dynamic linking, user-replaceable binaries, and a corresponding-source offer. Electing MPL-1.1 would have been lighter (file-level copyleft, no relinking obligation) but would add a second, differently-shaped set of obligations to track and release-gate.

$comment-completeness: EVERY dependency declared in vcpkg.json needs an entry here, even the obvious ones.
The audit must produce a verdict with NO installed vcpkg tree, because the CI gates job
has no vcpkg at all (D0-1) -- and without an entry, a component has no licence and
blocks. Relying on the SBOM alone would mean the licence gate only worked on machines
that had already built the dependency, which is precisely backwards.
Sources for the identifiers below: Tech-Stack-Plan.md 6.2.

leptonica.$note: Was https://leptonica.sourceforge.io/, which 302s to SourceForge's project-hosting page rather than serving the project (I-16, found by M-06). The upstream's own README names this repository as official; www.leptonica.org is the documentation site but serves no valid TLS, which is not a link to put in a licence document.

libjpeg-turbo.election: libjpeg-turbo is offered under IJG / BSD-3-Clause / zlib. We ELECT IJG, matching Tech-Stack-Plan.md 6.2.
